## Teaching points

1. A deep ulcer with exposed bone, an abnormal radiograph and inflammatory markers supports osteomyelitis. Assess perfusion and arrange infection and surgical review.
2. Minimal pain does not imply mild infection in a neuropathic foot.
3. Describe ulcer depth, surrounding infection and perfusion; arrange appropriate tissue or bone sampling and specialist source-control advice.
4. Antibiotics, pressure off-loading, glycemic management and wound follow-up are complementary. Radiographic bone changes do not disappear during the ED shift.
5. Tachycardia and leukocytosis meet two systemic inflammatory criteria, making this a severe diabetic foot infection in the IWGDF/IDSA classification despite preserved blood pressure. Begin IV antibiotics and arrange urgent surgical assessment.
